I study the fiscal, economic, and political impacts of domestic migratory waves, with a particular focus on the recent outmigration out of California caused by wildfires, pandemic, and high taxes. I take a quantitative approach to these questions, producing spatially granular panel datasets, and analyzing them with estimators conscious of dynamic trends. 


I also develop diagnostic and corrective tools for panel data analysis for more general settings, focusing on biases caused by parallel trend violations, composition changes between groups, and overlap violations. 


I also design messaging experiments to tease out American public reticence to energy infrastructure and heavy industry including data centers.
